rq: Can an action-conditioned runtime supervisor that models nearby people, carried-object dynamics, and observation-to-action delay reduce secondary physical hazards during humanoid task interruption, compared with strong stopping and semantic-fallback baselines, while preserving useful task completion?

task_definitions.T1: carry and place rigid box; person enters route
task_definitions.T2: shelf retrieval; person enters arm sweep

data_policy.split_unit: base scenario; disjoint layouts/object configurations/human trajectories as declared

design_rules.contact_threshold_source: E1 numerical validation; freeze at E5
design_rules.baseline_selection_rule: Among validated B1-B5 on development, minimize human hazard; break ties by safe success then latency. Declare tie tolerance before tuning. B0 is diagnostic only.
design_rules.missing_data_rule: Do not impute safety for missing outcomes. Retain failed attempts; confirmatory claims blocked until resolution or prespecified sensitivity analysis.
